title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan visits INA Museum at Moirang and Sainik School Imphal
subtitle:
Northeast is an integral and beautiful part of India; its people’s hard work and contribution are commendable: Vice-President
Sainik Schools have a special role in strengthening the spirit of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat: Vice-President
Do your duty every day to contribute to Viksit Bharat: Vice-President to Sainik School Imphal cadets
Vice President urges cadets to combine timeless values of patriotism and integrity with technological awareness and adaptability
body_text:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today visited the INA Museum at Moirang, Manipur paying homage to the valour and sacrifice of the Indian National Army (INA). He visited the historic site where the Indian Tricolour was first hoisted on the Indian mainland by the INA and toured the INA War Museum gallery. He also paid floral tribute to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, visited the INA Museum at Moirang, Manipur, today. Later, the Vice-President visited Sainik School Imphal, where he paid floral tribute at the War Memorial and was accorded a Guard of Honour by the cadets.
The Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan visited Sainik School Imphal, where he paid floral tribute at the War Memorial and was accorded a Guard of Honour by the cadets. He joined the cadets for lunch at the Mess and subsequently addressed and interacted with them. Addressing… pic.twitter.com/aslscwHTpM — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 8, 2026
Speaking on his visit to Moirang at the School, the Vice-President recalled the historic role of the INA in India’s freedom struggle. He noted that several freedom fighters from across the country, including many from Tamil Nadu, had joined the INA and made the supreme sacrifice for the nation. He also recalled his recent visit to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose had hoisted the Indian Tricolour, and said that these historic sites remind the younger generation of the courage, patriotism and sacrifices of India’s freedom fighters. The Vice-President emphasised that the true legacy of an institution is reflected not merely in its buildings or records, but in the character of its students and alumni. He called upon the cadets to particularly develop discipline, courage and leadership. “Even if you are less talented, with discipline you will shine,” Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said, stressing that discipline provides the foundation for excellence. On courage, he said that true courage also means standing up for others when someone is being unnecessarily harmed. On leadership, he emphasised that a true leader accepts responsibility, sets an example, listens to others and has the moral courage to take the right decision. Highlighting the importance of national integration, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that India’s diversity of languages, traditions and regions is united by a shared national identity. He said Sainik Schools have a special role in strengthening the spirit of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat, as students from diverse backgrounds learn, train, eat and play together. Referring to the rapid pace of technological change, he urged the cadets to preserve the timeless values of discipline, integrity and patriotism while also becoming adaptable, innovative and technologically aware. He mentioned emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, space technology, biotechnology, cybersecurity and robotics as areas offering new opportunities to the younger generation. During his interaction with the cadets, the Vice-President described the Northeast as an integral and beautiful part of India and praised the hard work and contribution of its people. He encouraged the students to retain their goodness while adapting themselves to change, observing that change is the only constant in the world. Responding to a question on his visit to Cellular Jail in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan encouraged the students to visit the historic site to understand the hardships endured by India’s freedom fighters. He said such a visit inspires patriotism and reminds the younger generation of the sacrifices made during the freedom struggle. On the role of students in building a developed India, the Vice-President said that every student can contribute by performing their duty to the best of their ability every day. He emphasised that doing one’s best each day would collectively contribute to the realisation of Viksit Bharat. The Vice-President was accompanied by Governor of Manipur Shri Ajay Kumar Bhalla, Chief Minister Shri Y. Khemchand Singh, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Defence Smt. Deepti Mohil Chawla, Major General Shubhankar Basu, VSM, Inspecting Officer, Sainik Schools Society, Ministry of Defence, Brigadier Amit Chatterjee, and Principal, Sainik School Imphal, Colonel A. Rajiv, among other dignitaries.
